```{r}
# A function that returns a data frame
create_df <- function(x) {
  tibble(value = x, squared = x^2, minus_2 = x - 2)
}

# Apply the function to a vector and row-bind the results
result_df <- map_dfr(1:3, create_df)
print(result_df)


result_df <- sapply(1:3, create_df)
print(result_df)
```

```{r}

age_function <- function(age_group){
  #create a temporary dataframe that contains a copy of the dataframe, but with a new column that will help us process only the age group we're interested in for one loop
  #effectively subsetting the dataframe into only this age group of interest
  tmp <- df_tp |> mutate(indicator = susp_age_group == age_group) #create a column that indicates whether the row has the age group we're interested in
  print(tmp)
  
  #conduct a t-test for that age-group against the time period
  #ie for a given age group, is their proportion of 
  print(as.numeric(tmp$indicator)) #change the boolean values to 1/0 values
  
  tt  <- t.test(as.numeric(indicator) ~ time_period, #as.numeric(indicator) tells us the average of people in that age group who did commit crime. compare this before vs. after
                data = tmp,
                alternative = "greater")  # after > before
  
  broom::tidy(tt) |>
    mutate(
      susp_age_group = age_group,
      n_before = sum(tmp$time_period == "before Patternizr"),
      n_after  = sum(tmp$time_period == "after Patternizr")
    )
}

map_dfr(c("25-44"), age_function)

#age_ttests_top
```

write out methodology and why filtered data the way i did.

```{r}
library(broom)

df_tp <- df |>
  filter(precinct_crime %in% top_precincts,
         time_period %in% c("before Patternizr", "after Patternizr")) |>
  mutate(time_period = factor(time_period,
                              levels = c("after Patternizr", "before Patternizr")))

age_levels <- df_tp |> distinct(susp_age_group) |> pull()

age_ttests_by_precinct <- df_tp |>
  group_by(precinct_crime) |>
  group_modify(~ map_dfr(age_levels, function(ag) {
    tmp <- .x |> mutate(ind = susp_age_group == ag)
    tt  <- t.test(as.numeric(ind) ~ time_period, data = tmp, alternative = "greater")
    broom::tidy(tt) |>
      mutate(
        susp_age_group = ag,
        n_after  = sum(tmp$time_period == "after Patternizr"),
        n_before = sum(tmp$time_period == "before Patternizr")
      )
  })) |>
  ungroup()

age_ttests_by_precinct
age_ttests_by_precinct |> select(precinct_crime, susp_age_group, estimate, p.value)

write.csv(age_ttests_by_precinct, "age_precinct_t-tests.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```



```{r}
### RE-WRITTEN BY LLM WHILE TRYING TO UNDERSTAND FOR SEX DEMOGRAPHIC


# --- STEP 1: PREPARE DATA ---
# Filter for Top Precincts and valid Time Periods
df_tp <- df |>
  filter(precinct_crime %in% top_precincts,
         time_period %in% c("before Patternizr", "after Patternizr"))
df_tp #creates a dataframe with only top 20 precincts and no null/no unknown values for age group

# Get the list of unique age groups to loop through
age_levels <- unique(df_tp$susp_age_group)
age_levels #creates list of all unique age group levels

# Create a list to store our results
results_list <- list()

# --- STEP 2: THE EXPLICIT LOOP ---

for (current_age_group in age_levels) {
  
  # A. MANUALLY SPLIT THE DATAFRAME
  # Create two completely separate tables
  before_df <- filter(df_tp, time_period == "before Patternizr")
  after_df  <- filter(df_tp, time_period == "after Patternizr")
  
  # B. CREATE A VECTOR CONTAINING BINARY INDICATOR OF IF ROW IS IN AGE GROUP OF INTEREST (THE 0s and 1s)
  # For the "Before" pile: 1 if it matches the current age group, 0 if not
  age_interest_before <- as.numeric(before_df$susp_age_group == current_age_group)
  #before patternizr, WHICH people in this age group committed crime?
  
  # For the "After" pile: 1 if it matches the current age group, 0 if not
  age_interest_after  <- as.numeric(after_df$susp_age_group == current_age_group)
  #after patternizr, WHICH people in this age group committed crime?
  
  # --- CONCEPT CHECK: PROVING MEAN = PROPORTION ---
  # If vec_before is c(1, 1, 0, 0), the mean is 0.5 (50%)
  # This calculates the actual % of crimes committed by this age group
  prop_age_interest_before <- mean(age_interest_before) 
  #before patternizr, what proportion of people in this age group committed crime relative to people not in this age group?
  print(prop_age_interest_before)
  prop_age_interest_after  <- mean(age_interest_after)
  #after patternizr, what proportion of people in this age group comitted crime relative to people not in this age group?
  print(prop_age_interest_after)
  
  # C. RUN THE T-TEST ON THE TWO VECTORS
  # We compare the "After" vector against the "Before" vector
  tt <- t.test(age_interest_after, age_interest_before, alternative = "greater")
  print(tt)
  
  # D. SAVE RESULTS
  results_list[[current_age_group]] <- data.frame(
    age_group      = current_age_group,
    # These 'estimates' from the t-test will match the means we calculated above!
    prop_before    = tt$estimate[2], 
    prop_after     = tt$estimate[1],
    p_value        = tt$p.value,
    n_before       = length(vec_before), # Total crimes in 'before' period
    n_after        = length(vec_after)   # Total crimes in 'after' period
  )
}
print(results_list)

# --- STEP 3: COMBINE RESULTS ---
final_results <- bind_rows(results_list)

# View the table
print(final_results)
```
